node_modifiers.label: string <= 400 characters
node_modifiers.mask: a mask expression, at most one per node

mix.doc: blend of the node's result with its input; keyframable

node_modifiers.off: bypass the node (passes its input through)

notes: targets.lut is per op; a mask with blur_px > 0, keyframes, or any non-pointwise node makes the whole program not LUT-expressible. targets.dctl excludes blurred mattes and depth / segment masks.

blur.doc: Gaussian blur of the working values.

cdl.doc: ASC CDL on ACEScct code values, unclamped (CLF 'FwdNoClamp'): v = in * slope + offset; v = v ** power where v >= 0; then saturation around Rec.709 luma.

contrast.doc: Log contrast around a pivot: out = (in - pivot) * amount + pivot.

curve.doc: Monotone cubic curve (Fritsch-Carlson, no overshoot) through points; straight lines with the end slopes beyond. channel luma keeps colour (adds the luma change to all channels); rgb applies to each channel. space log: points are ACEScct code values; display: on-screen sRGB code values.

density.doc: Subtractive (film-like) colour density: darkens each pixel by amount times its opponent chroma, so saturated colours get deeper rather than brighter. 0.5 subtle, 1.5 strong.

diffusion.doc: Diffusion / mist filter: light from bright areas spreads into darker neighbours (adds max(blur - in, 0) in linear light); lowers local contrast round highlights.

exposure.doc: Exposure: a linear-light gain (decode ACEScct, multiply by 2^stops, encode); above the toe it is the same as adding stops / 17.52, and it never lifts black below the toe.

gamut_compress.doc: Reference gamut compression (the open ACES method) on linear AP1: pulls colours outside the gamut back in along their distance from the achromatic axis, leaving colours inside threshold untouched.

limit.doc: [cyan, magenta, yellow] distance mapped to the gamut boundary

threshold.doc: [cyan, magenta, yellow] distance where compression starts

glow.doc: Bloom: light above `threshold` (cv) spreads by a Gaussian of `radius_px` and is added back in linear light, `warm` tints the halo.

threshold.doc: level where glow starts (0.6 ~ 3.4 stops over grey)

grain.doc: Deterministic film-like grain: value noise on a `size_px` lattice from an integer hash of (cell, frame, seed, channel), strongest in the mid-tones. Same seed + frame = the same random cells on every target (grain values within float tolerance).

guided_detail.doc: Edge-aware detail on luma (guided filter): edges stronger than `edge` keep their shape, so no halos; amount > 0 crisper texture, < 0 smoother.

edge.doc: luma step treated as an edge (sqrt of the filter's eps)

radius_px.doc: box radius of the guided filter

halation.doc: Film-style halation: like glow, but the halo is tinted (default red-orange) and starts lower; light scattered back from the film base round bright edges.

highlights_shadows.doc: Local tone from a blurred luma: highlights < 0 pulls bright areas down, shadows > 0 opens dark areas. 1.0 = 0.1 cv at full strength.

hue_rotate.doc: Rotates every hue by the same angle (opponent Cb / Cr plane).

hue_vs_hue.doc: Rotate selected hues. Each point [hue, shift, width] acts with a raised-cosine influence `width` degrees each side (default 60); overlapping points blend. Hue is the angle of (Cb, Cr) of the ACEScct working values, degrees: red ~123, skin ~141, orange ~150, yellow ~173, green ~206, cyan ~300, blue ~350, magenta ~60.

hue_vs_lum.doc: Brightness by hue (cv offset, weighted by chroma so greys stay): points [hue, offset, width]. 0.03 is clearly visible. Hue is the angle of (Cb, Cr) of the ACEScct working values, degrees: red ~123, skin ~141, orange ~150, yellow ~173, green ~206, cyan ~300, blue ~350, magenta ~60.

hue_vs_sat.doc: Saturation by hue: points [hue, gain, width]; gain 1 = unchanged. Hue is the angle of (Cb, Cr) of the ACEScct working values, degrees: red ~123, skin ~141, orange ~150, yellow ~173, green ~206, cyan ~300, blue ~350, magenta ~60.

local_contrast.doc: Wide-radius local contrast on luma, blacks protected.

lum_vs_sat.doc: Saturation by luma: monotone curve [[luma, gain], ...] over ACEScct luma (0.15 deep shadow, 0.41 grey, 0.6 bright, 0.75+ highlights).

photo_to_scene.doc: Display-referred photo (sRGB JPEG / PNG read as linear light) back to scene light through the inverse ACES 2.0 SDR sRGB output transform, so the program's ACES 2.0 output gives the photo's own placement back. Highlights roll off from knee_stops to max_stops over grey. Allowed only in photo_graph.

recovered_highlights.doc: keep stops over display white where every channel is > 1 (only linear_photo input can exceed 1; srgb_photo and rec1886_photo are clipped)

printer_lights.doc: Film-lab printer points: 1 point = 0.025 log10 exposure (~1/12 stop) per channel.

rgb_mixer.doc: Channel mixer on the working values: out = M·in with rows red, green, blue ([1, 0, 0] etc. = unchanged); preserve_luma keeps each pixel's luma.

preserve_luma.doc: add back the luma the mix changed

sat_vs_lum.doc: Luma by saturation: monotone curve [[chroma, offset], ...] adds offset (cv) to the luma of colours of that chroma (negative darkens saturated colours).

sat_vs_sat.doc: Remap opponent chroma: monotone curve [[chroma_in, chroma_out], ...] (0.05 moderate, 0.1+ strong).

saturation.doc: Saturation: scales opponent chroma (Cb, Cr) of the working values. protect_skin 0..1 keeps skin hues (141 +- 15..40 deg) near their own saturation.

sharpen.doc: Unsharp mask on luma with noise coring (detail below `coring` is left alone).

split_tone.doc: Tints shadows and highlights toward two hues (opponent-plane offsets weighted by luma), balance moves the split point.

vibrance.doc: Saturation weighted toward muted colours: k = 1 + amount · (1 − smoothstep(0, 0.12, C)); already saturated colours move little.

vignette.doc: Darken (amount > 0) or brighten (< 0) the frame edges. 0.1 subtle, 0.3 strong.

wheels.doc: Lift / gamma / gain / offset colour wheels as ACEScct offsets weighted by soft tonal ranges of luma (shadows, mids, highlights). 0.01 cv is a visible tint, 0.03 strong.

white_balance.doc: Temperature / tint as linear-light gains per AP1 channel, in stops: decode, multiply by 2^[temperature, -tint, -temperature], encode (above the toe the same as adding [...] / 17.52).

aces2.doc: ACES 2.0 output transform (OpenColorIO built-in ACES 2.0 studio config): SDR 100-nit Rec.709 on an sRGB or Rec.1886 (gamma 2.4) display, SDR P3-D65 (Display P3 or DCI-style P3-D65), or HDR: PQ (Rec.2100) at 1000 / 2000 / 4000 nits in P3-D65 or Rec.2020, HLG at 1000 nits. The grading loop measures on SDR Rec.709 only.

acescct.doc: No output transform: ACEScct code values out (an LMT).

display_encode.doc: Working values to Rec.709 linear, saturated colours above 0.9 soft-compressed toward their luminance, then the display encoding. No tone scale.
